findings.evidence: The precedent this PR copies names both sides: `FiniteType.lean:152 noncomputable def finiteTypeCommHopfAlgCatOpEquivFiniteTypeAffineGroupSchemeCat … : (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} R)ᵒᵖ ≌ FiniteTypeAffineGroupSchemeCat (CommRingCat.of R)`, with `FiniteType.lean:166/179` carrying the same doubled prefix. Naming conventions: the name describes the conclusion, and consistency with adjacent declarations governs.
findings.fix: Rename to `geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgCatOpEquivGeometricallyConnectedAffineGroupSchemeCat`, with the private helper and the `functorCompιIso` namespace following, and update line 31.
findings.issue: `geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgCatOpEquivAffineGroupSchemeCat` qualifies only the Hopf-algebra side; the target is `GeometricallyConnectedAffineGroupSchemeCat (CommRingCat.of k)`, not `AffineGroupSchemeCat`. Read against the existing unrestricted `commHopfAlgCatOpEquivAffineGroupSchemeCat` (Equivalence.lean:37), the name says "geometrically connected Hopf algebras ≌ all affine group schemes", which is a false statement. The same defect is in the derived names at lines 166 (`…AffineGroupSchemeCatFunctorCompιIso`) and 178 (`…AffineGroupSchemeCat.functorCompιIso`), and in the module-doc entry at line 31.

findings.evidence: Line 157: `GeometricallyConnectedAffineGroupSchemeCat (CommRingCat.of k)`; line 59 `(S : CommRingCat.{u})`. The precedent header writes it correctly: `FiniteType.lean:26 "(FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat R)ᵒᵖ ≌ FiniteTypeAffineGroupSchemeCat (CommRingCat.of R)"`.
findings.issue: The module-header display `GeometricallyConnectedAffineGroupSchemeCat (Spec k)` misstates the argument: the declaration takes a `CommRingCat`, not a scheme, so the displayed statement does not typecheck.

summary: The restricted anti-equivalence and its two derived isomorphisms name only the source side as geometrically connected, so the names assert an equivalence with the full `AffineGroupSchemeCat` — a statement stronger than (and false for) what is proved — and break the naming pattern of the adjacent finite-type restriction.
